steps: The Planer performs a planing operation on the MilledPart, which is delivered by the MobileRobot, removing material to a depth of 3.5 mm with a feed rate of 0.25 mm/rev to achieve a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, taking 57 minutes to complete, and outputs the resulting PlanedPart onto the ConveyorBelt.

On a Broaching Machine, a pull broach is used to perform a broaching operation on a MetalBar loaded from a MobileRobot, cutting to a depth of 2.8 mm at a feed rate of 0.18 mm/stroke, producing a BroachedComponent that is placed on a ConveyorBelt, and the operation takes 18 minutes.

The Stewart Platform Mills performs precision milling on the MilledPart for 44 minutes using a 6-flute carbide end mill with a milling precision of ±0.005 mm and an active damping system engaged, transforming the input component into a GroundPart that is then transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

A surface grinding operation is performed on a PlanedPart using a Grinding Machines, employing an aluminum oxide grinding wheel with 60 grit at a wheel speed of 3200 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/pass, lasting for 17 minutes, to produce a GroundPart that is then placed on a MobileRobot.

On a Vertical Lathe, a metal bar is subjected to vertical turning for 66 minutes, using a carbide insert tool (CNMG 1204) at a spindle speed of 450 rpm and a feed rate of 0.2 mm/rev, resulting in a lathed part that is transferred to a conveyor belt.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs wire EDM cutting on the GroundPart for 34 minutes using deionized water as the dielectric fluid, fine finish mode, and automatic edge deburring, resulting in a PrecisionFinishedPart that is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

The Laser Cutter performs laser cutting on a sheet metal component loaded by a mobile robot, using a 3000 W laser with nitrogen gas assist at 18 bar and a cutting speed of 2.1 m/min, operating for 83 minutes to produce a cut sheet metal part that is then transferred to a conveyor belt.

Using a Bandsaw, cold sawing is performed on a MetalBar loaded from a MobileRobot for 76 minutes at a saw speed of 60 m/min with a bi-metal variable pitch blade and a cutting width of 3 mm, resulting in a LathedPart delivered to a ConveyorBelt.

Using a Drill Press, a MetalBar is drilled with a 12 mm drill at a spindle speed of 850 rpm and a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev for 66 minutes, resulting in a DrilledComponent that is placed on a ConveyorBelt.

On a Screw Machines, perform Screw Threading on LathedPart components received from a MobileRobot, producing ScrewedComponent parts at a rate of 120 parts per hour using M10 screw size with Metric coarse thread type, and transfer the finished components to a ConveyorBelt, taking 20 minutes.

On the CNC Turning Center, a CNC turning operation is performed on the LathedPart for 94 minutes, using CNC program Program_07B with verified and loaded tool offsets and a spindle speed of 1200 rpm, resulting in the production of the FinishedMachinedComponent, which is then placed on the ConveyorBelt.

The Honing Machine performs a honing operation on the HonedCylinder, using a 220 grit honing stone to achieve a bore size of 45.0 ± 0.002 mm, lasting for 67 minutes, after which the resulting PrecisionFinishedPart is transferred to the ConveyorBelt.

Using a horizontal milling machine, a horizontal milling operation is performed on the MilledPart loaded by the MobileRobot, machining the part for 76 minutes at a milling speed of 280 m/min using a climb milling tool path to achieve a surface finish of Ra 0.8 µm, resulting in the finished machined component being placed on the ConveyorBelt.

The Shaper performs a shaping operation on the MilledPart, using an HSS single-point tool with a stroke length of 150 mm and a shaping speed of 25 strokes per minute, for 1 minute, transforming it into a ShapedPart that is then placed on the ConveyorBelt.

The Shear (Sheet Metal) machine performs a shearing operation on sheet metal material delivered by a MobileRobot, cutting it into cut sheet metal pieces using a tungsten carbide edge blade with a shear angle of 2.5 degrees and a cutting speed of 1 cut every 12 seconds, running for 84 minutes, and transferring the resulting ShearedSheetMetal to a ConveyorBelt.

Using a Punch Press, a sheet metal component is punched with a 25 mm round punch at a stroke speed of 80 strokes per minute and laser-aligned die setup, transforming the input sheet metal into a finished sheet metal product that is then transferred to a conveyor belt, all within a processing duration of 31 minutes.

A lathed part is milled using a vertical milling machine through a vertical milling operation at a milling speed of 320 m/min with a 4-flute end mill tool and a depth of cut of 4 mm, lasting for 78 minutes, resulting in a milled part that is then placed on a conveyor belt.

On a Hobbing Machine, a gear hobbing operation is performed on a BroachedComponent loaded from a MobileRobot, using a hobbing speed of 180 rpm and a feed rate of 0.5 mm/rev to cut an involute gear profile with a 20° pressure angle, lasting for 16 minutes, resulting in a HobbiedGear that is transferred to a ConveyorBelt.

On a Horizontal Lathe, a MetalBar is turned into a LathedPart through a turning operation lasting 15 minutes, using a CNMG 1204 carbide tool at a rotation speed of 500 rpm and a feed rate of 0.18 mm/rev, with the finished part transferred to a ConveyorBelt upon completion.

On the Gear Shaper, a broached component is shaped into a spur gear with 36 teeth using a shaping speed of 160 strokes per minute, resulting in a shaped gear, and the operation runs for 91 minutes before the output is placed on the ConveyorBelt.

On the Gear Shaper machine, a broached component is shaped into a spur gear with 24 teeth through the gear shaping operation at a speed of 120 strokes per minute, taking 56 minutes to complete, after which the resulting shaped gear is placed on a conveyor belt.

The Bandsaw performs a bar cutting operation on a metal bar loaded from a MobileRobot, using a bi-metal variable pitch blade at a saw speed of 60 meters per minute and a cutting width of 3 mm, taking 91 minutes to complete, and resulting in a lathed part delivered to a ConveyorBelt.

The Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machine) performs precision wire cutting on the shaped part, using a 0.25 mm brass-coated wire and high precision finishing pulse electrical parameters at a cutting speed of 8 mm² per minute, resulting in a precision finished part, and the operation runs for 62 minutes before the output is placed on the ConveyorBelt.
